channel.title: Patch Dispatch
channel.description: Patch it before they dispatch it. Every vulnerability here is already being exploited in the wild: Windows, Linux, PHP, npm, Python and enterprise software.

item.title: Drupal Core Installer Takeover Vulnerability (CVE-2026-136716) — Unauthenticated Site Compromise
item.description: Summary Drupal Core’s installer can be abused by an unauthenticated remote attacker to fully take over a site, when that site is left in an unusual or incomplete installation state with install.php reachable. This is not a brand-new category of bug: it follows a related installer flaw fixed in SA-CORE-2026-017, and sites that patched that one but left the installer exposed, or that never fully completed installation, can still be hit by this one. CISA added it to the KEV catalog on 2026-11-27, one day after publication, confirming active exploitation — anyone running Drupal should treat this as urgent.

item.title: Mitel MiCollab Unauthenticated OS Command Injection (CVE-2026-133323)
item.description: Summary Mitel MiCollab’s Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component fails to sanitize input properly, letting an unauthenticated attacker inject OS commands over the network with no login and no user interaction needed. This is a fresh flaw, confirmed under active exploitation within days of being published — anyone running MiCollab with AWV reachable from outside should treat this as urgent. Public proof-of-concept exploit code and a scanner tool are already circulating, which lowers the bar for attackers significantly.

item.title: Drupal Core Installer Flaw Allows Unauthenticated Site Takeover (CVE-2026-132165)
item.description: Summary Drupal Core’s installer script (install.php) can be abused by an unauthenticated attacker to trigger a reinstall of the site, which can lead to full site takeover or remote code execution. CISA added this to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on November 24, 2026, confirming active exploitation in the wild. If you run Drupal and haven’t locked down install.php, treat this as urgent. Note: as of this writing, NVD and OSV have no published record for this CVE, and the vendor advisory could not be independently verified through our usual channels. The version numbers and dates below come from our research brief and have not been cross-checked against an independently accessible official source — verify them against your own Drupal update channel before acting on exact version strings.

item.title: Xen Orchestra Authentication Bypass via Empty-Object Token Cookie (CVE-2026-133469)
item.description: Timeline of updates 27 November 2026 What changed: 5.211.2 is an available patched version for the 5.2xx branch; users need not upgrade directly to 6.9.2. Affected versions should clarify the separate 5.2xx vulnerability range (up to 5.211.1) distinct from 5.213.x. Affected versions now: Branch Status 5.0.0 – 5.211.1 Vulnerable 5.211.2 Fixed 5.213.0, 5.213.1 Vulnerable (no fix on this branch — move to 6.9.2+) 6.0.0 – 6.9.1 Vulnerable 6.9.2 Fixed 6.10.0 Vulnerable 6.10.1 Fixed Note the 5.2xx line has two separate vulnerable ranges: versions up to 5.211.1 are fixed by upgrading to 5.211.2, but 5.213.0 and 5.213.1 have no patched release on that branch — those installs must move to 6.9.2 or 6.10.1 instead.

item.title: Mitel MiCollab XML Injection Lets Attackers Run Commands Unauthenticated (CVE-2026-133303)
item.description: Summary Mitel MiCollab’s Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component has an XML injection flaw that lets an unauthenticated attacker run arbitrary commands on the system by feeding it pre-staged malicious content. CISA confirmed active exploitation on November 25, 2026, just days after the CVE was published (November 19, 2026), so this is a freshly disclosed and freshly exploited issue, not an old bug resurfacing. Anyone running MiCollab with AWV reachable from untrusted networks, especially the internet, should treat this as urgent.

item.title: Mitel MiCollab Authentication Bypass in Conferencing Component (CVE-2026-133324)
item.description: Summary Mitel MiCollab’s Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component fails to fail securely when handling authentication, letting an unauthenticated attacker bypass login controls and perform unauthorized actions. CISA confirmed active exploitation on November 25, 2026, days after the CVE was published, so this is a fresh, actively-targeted flaw, not an old one resurfacing. Anyone running MiCollab with AWV reachable from untrusted networks should treat this as urgent. Affected versions All MiCollab versions through 10.3.0.18 are vulnerable. We do not have a confirmed patched build number from Mitel at this time — our information stops at “through 10.3.0.18” and does not state a fixed version.

item.title: Danfoss AK-SM 800A Series Authentication Bypass (CVE-2025-41450)
item.description: Summary Danfoss AK-SM 800A Series refrigeration controllers can be tricked into generating a web report without any valid login, leaking internal IP addresses, usernames, and store names. The bug relies on a hidden “code-of-the-day” mechanism that derives a valid password from the device’s current date, which an attacker can reproduce and use against the xml.cgi?action=getauth endpoint. This is a known flaw with a fix available since March 2025, but CISA confirmed active exploitation only in November 2026 — if you run these controllers, assume someone may already be probing them, and public PoC/detection tooling (FROMAGEGATE) is circulating.

item.title: Danfoss AK-SM 800A Path Traversal Flaw (CVE-2023-25914) Now Under Active Attack
item.description: Summary A path traversal bug in the XML interface of Danfoss AK-SM 800A refrigeration controllers lets an authenticated attacker read arbitrary files off the underlying server, including configuration and credential data that can lead to full system compromise. This flaw has been known since August 2023, but CISA confirmed active exploitation only in November 2026 — if you run this hardware, don’t assume it’s old news. Affected versions Firmware | Status 3.3 and earlier | Vulnerable 3.4 and later | Fixed

item.title: Danfoss AK-SM 800A Command Injection via Input Validation Flaw (CVE-2023-25915)
item.description: Summary Danfoss AK-SM 800A Series refrigeration/automation controllers let an authenticated remote attacker run arbitrary commands due to improper input validation in the firmware. This flaw has been known since 2023, but CISA confirmed active exploitation only in November 2026, so systems that were never patched have likely been sitting exposed for years. Anyone running these controllers, especially with any form of remote or network access, should treat this as urgent.

item.title: SAP NetWeaver JNDI Injection Flaw (CVE-2025-42884) Under Active Exploitation
item.description: Summary SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal 7.50 fails to properly sanitize input used in JNDI lookup operations, letting an unauthenticated attacker inject JNDI environment properties or a crafted lookup URL to redirect the server to an unintended JNDI provider. CISA added this to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-20, confirming it is being actively exploited now. Anyone running NetWeaver Enterprise Portal, especially with any network or internet exposure, should treat this as urgent.

item.title: Cisco BroadWorks XXE Flaw Lets Attackers Read Server Files Unauthenticated (CVE-2026-20320)
item.description: Summary Cisco BroadWorks’ OCI-P provisioning service parses XML without disabling external entity resolution, so a crafted XML message lets an unauthenticated remote attacker read arbitrary files off the server’s filesystem with the privileges of the BroadWorks process. Cisco shipped a fix in August 2026, and CISA added this to its exploited-vulnerabilities list in November 2026 — if you run BroadWorks and haven’t patched, treat this as urgent. Anyone operating BroadWorks Application Delivery Platform, Application Server, Profile Server, or Xtended Services Platform exposed to untrusted networks should check their version today.

item.title: VMware vCenter Authentication Bypass (CVE-2026-123890) — Unauthenticated Full Compromise
item.description: Summary VMware vCenter has a critical authentication bypass in the VMware Directory Service: an attacker with network access to vCenter, with no credentials and no user interaction, can bypass login entirely and gain unauthorized access. This affects standalone vCenter as well as vCenter bundled inside VMware Cloud Foundation, vSphere Foundation, and Telco Cloud Platform/Infrastructure. CISA added this to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-20, meaning it is being actively exploited in the wild — this is current activity, not a years-old flaw resurfacing.

item.title: N-able MailAssure SSRF Lets High-Privilege API Users Probe Your Internal Network (CVE-2026-134624)
item.description: Summary N-able MailAssure (SpamExperts) has a server-side request forgery flaw in its LDAP synchronization connection check: it doesn’t restrict which hosts or ports the server can connect to. An API user with high-level privileges can abuse this to make the MailAssure server connect to arbitrary internal hosts, map out what’s reachable, and send crafted data to internal services. CISA confirms active exploitation, so if you run MailAssure with LDAP relay configured and don’t tightly control who holds elevated API credentials, this is worth acting on now.

item.title: IBM Aspera Faspex Authorization Bypass Lets Users Become Admins (CVE-2026-123218)
item.description: Summary IBM Aspera Faspex has a flaw that lets any logged-in user craft a specific message to bypass authorization checks and grab full administrative privileges. This is not a years-old bug resurfacing — the fix came out October 26, 2026, and CISA added it to the exploited list shortly after, on November 9, 2026, so attacks are following close behind the patch release. If you run Faspex for managed file transfer, treat this as urgent: any authenticated account, even a low-privilege one, can be turned into an admin.

item.title: Cisco Expressway Series Hard-Coded Credentials Let Root Commands Run via Cluster Database (CVE-2026-76466)
item.description: Summary Cisco Expressway Core (Expressway-C) and Expressway Edge (Expressway-E) devices running in a cluster have a flaw in their database service: it relies on persistent cookies that aren’t properly validated, and when TLS Verify Mode is set to Enabled for clustering, client certificates aren’t actually checked. An attacker who gets hold of a valid persistent cookie can talk to the database service directly and run arbitrary RPC commands, which translates into arbitrary OS commands as root on the device. This CVE was added to CISA’s KEV catalog on 2026-11-20; Cisco itself says it has no direct evidence of active exploitation but is not disputing the listing.

item.title: PHP Stale Request-State Remote Code Execution (CVE-2026-109619)

item.title: PHP Memory Corruption via OOM longjmp() Leads to Remote Code Execution (CVE-2026-109618)
item.description: Summary PHP mishandles out-of-memory conditions: when an allocation fails mid-request, PHP uses longjmp() to bail out of the current context, but request memory can be left uninitialized before the shutdown procedure runs. That shutdown code then reads or branches on the bad memory, giving an unauthenticated attacker a path to remote code execution. This is actively exploited in the wild, and anyone running PHP under Apache mod_php or FrankenPHP should treat this as urgent.

item.title: Linux Kernel ESP Shared-Fragment Flaw Enables Root Escalation (CVE-2026-46300)
item.description: Updated (24 Nov 2026): RHEL 10 received a newer kernel update: kernel-6.12.0-211.16.1.el10_2 (RHSA-2026:19569) supersedes the original kernel-6.12.0-211.8.el10nv fix. Summary A bug in the kernel’s skb_try_coalesce() function drops a safety marker that tells the IPsec ESP code whether a socket buffer contains shared, page-cache-backed memory. When that marker is lost, ESP decrypts traffic in place over fragments it shouldn’t touch, corrupting page-cache data. On its own this is a data-integrity bug, but CISA confirms it’s being actively exploited in the wild, chained with two other flaws (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) to plant PHP webshells and get root. Anyone running IPsec/ESP with TCP receive coalescing enabled should treat this as urgent.

item.title: Apache Roller Unauthenticated RCE via XML-RPC Deserialization (CVE-2026-129448)
item.description: Summary Apache Roller’s XML-RPC endpoint deserializes vendor extension types in incoming requests before it checks whether the caller is authenticated, letting an unauthenticated remote attacker achieve code execution. This is a current flaw with a fix released September 2026, and CISA confirms it is being actively exploited as of November 20, 2026 — treat it as urgent, not as old news. If you run Roller for blogging/CMS on a Java application server (e.g., Tomcat), this affects you directly.

item.title: Outlook Spoofing Flaw Skips User Warnings — CVE-2026-124194
item.description: Updated (24 Nov 2026): MSRC confirms fixed build versions are available: 16.0.17932.21140 (for one product stream) and 16.0.14334.21048 (for another), contradicting the previous brief’s ’not stated’ for fixed_versions. MSRC confirms the vulnerability was released on 2026-11-10 with security updates available via aka.ms/OfficeSecurityReleases, providing a concrete patching reference. Summary Microsoft Outlook fails to show a warning dialog before performing an unsafe action, letting an attacker craft emails that spoof content or sender context without tipping off the recipient. This is being actively exploited now, so anyone running Outlook via Microsoft 365 Apps or the LTSC releases should treat this as a patch-now item, not a backlog ticket.

item.title: OpenSSH on Alpine and other musl Linux: password check can be bypassed (CVE-2026-123158)
item.description: Updated (24 Nov 2026): The fixed versions table is incomplete; Alpine provides fixed packages for branches 3.16 through 3.20, which should be added to the table (3.20: 9.7_p1-r6, 3.19: 9.6_p1-r3, 3.18: 9.3_p2-r4, 3.17: 9.1_p1-r7, 3.16: 9.0_p1-r6). Updated (22 Nov 2026): expanded with the affected conditions, fixed versions and fix steps from the OpenSSH, musl and Alpine advisories. The first version only said that affected versions were not stated. Summary On some Linux servers, OpenSSH lets an attacker log in to accounts that have no password set, such as accounts meant for key-only access. The bug affects systems built on the musl C library, Alpine Linux being the best-known example, when sshd checks passwords itself instead of through PAM. CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 9 November 2026, so it is being used in real attacks.

item.title: BerriAI LiteLLM Remote Code Execution via Unprotected Alternate Channel (CVE-2026-40217)
item.description: Updated (24 Nov 2026): Fixed version is now known: LiteLLM 1.83.10 (or 1.83.11) patched the vulnerability; affected range is 1.81.8 through 1.83.9. CVSS score clarification: NVD reports 8.8 (CVSS:3.1); GitHub advisory reports 5.9 (CVSS v4), indicating a significant scoring discrepancy between frameworks. Attack vector clarified: requires proxy-admin credential in default configurations, not unauthenticated remote access as the NVD description might imply. Workaround documented: block POST /guardrails/test_custom_code at reverse proxy or API gateway if immediate upgrade is not possible.
